title: Fallopian tube X-ray (HSG)
what: Contrast dye is passed through the cervix, and X-rays are taken. They show the shape of the uterus and whether the tubes are open.
why: For trouble getting pregnant, before infertility treatment, or after surgery on the tubes.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; results often right after the images
tell_doctor: If you might be pregnant. The procedure is not done then
Allergy to iodine or contrast dye
Inflammation, discharge, or pain low in the belly now or recently

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: Usually in the first half of the cycle: after your period ends and before ovulation, often day 6 to 12. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually a vaginal swab for infections is needed, sometimes a blood test. The clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Pregnancy
prepare.text: Pregnancy is ruled out before the procedure. Sometimes you are asked to take a test, or not to try to conceive in this cycle before the HSG.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: Ask your doctor if you can take a painkiller 30 to 60 minutes before.

bring: Someone with you, if you feel nervous
steps: You lie on the table, as for a gynecological exam
The doctor inserts a speculum and cleans the cervix
A thin tube is placed in the cervix
Contrast is slowly passed through it
The tube and speculum are removed
feel: Cramps low in the belly, like period pain, while the contrast goes in
The feelings usually pass in a few minutes or hours
after: You may have spotting for a few days. Use a pad
Usually no sex, swimming pools, or baths for 1 to 2 days. Ask your doctor
Go over the results with your gynecologist or fertility doctor
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), severe pain low in the belly, or bad-smelling discharge: call your doctor
Heavy bleeding or fainting: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually it feels like period cramps. Tell the doctor if it hurts a lot. They can pause.

faq.q: Can I get pregnant in the same cycle after an HSG?
faq.a: Ask your doctor. Often trying is allowed in the same cycle, but clinics have different rules.

reminders.text: Fallopian tube X-ray tomorrow. Bring your swab results, tests, and a sanitary pad.
